questions.stem: An L-shaped figure can be split into a $10\text{ cm} \times 4\text{ cm}$ rectangle and a $6\text{ cm} \times 3\text{ cm}$ rectangle. What is the total area?
What is the first step in finding the area of a compound shape?

options.text: Split it into simpler shapes whose areas you can calculate
Find the perimeter first, then square it
Estimate the area by counting squares

questions.explanation: To find the area of a compound shape, split (or decompose) it into simpler shapes such as rectangles, triangles, or trapeziums, then add or subtract their areas.
